name: Para-fascism
summary: Para-fascism is Roger Griffin's term for conservative and military dictatorships of the interwar years that copied the outward features of Italian Fascism and Nazism (leader cult, state party, youth and paramilitary organisations, ritual politics) without its revolutionary drive to create a new society. Such regimes lean on tradition, elites and the church, treat communism as the main enemy and move to neutralise genuine fascist movements once they no longer need them. Its sources define a type of regime, so they speak to few of the test's questions.

scope: The analytic category Griffin coined in The Nature of Fascism (1993) and developed with Kallis, Costa Pinto and others: interwar authoritarian conservative regimes that imitated fascist trappings without fascism's revolutionary palingenetic nationalism, with Salazar's Estado Novo as the best-documented case in the sources read. It excludes genuine fascism and the individual regimes' own doctrines (Salazarism, Francoism, Austrofascism), which are other subjects; their texts are not used.
